The width of the confidence intervals (the "90% CI") reflects uncertainty, which grows as the forecast horizon lengthens. For 1 day, the range between 327.85 and 333.15 is tight because of the limited time available for variability to take hold. Within a week, volatility has more time to compound, so the range broadens to 322.5–339.5, considering potential daily fluctuations or unexpected deviations from the base trend. However, no model can capture every potential risk, and there are always events that could push outcomes outside your intervals. For example, sudden shocks such as a major geopolitical event, an unexpected change in market regulations, or a surprise data release could drive extreme values. Similarly, if the prediction relates to markets, shifts in investor sentiment or unexpected macroeconomic announcements could lead to abrupt deviations. These risks highlight the limitations of probabilistic forecasting, even while the provided estimates and intervals aim to represent the most likely outcomes under typical conditions.
